prompts.static_initial:

Asset type: one static character sprite candidate for a 2D isometric game, not a concept redesign.
Input image 1 is the approved full-body character identity. Input image 2 is the eight-direction standing sheet; use ONLY the SECOND character from the left as the exact camera, pose and silhouette reference (screen southwest, three-quarter front facing down-left).
Create a single isolated full-body character in precisely that second reference view. Preserve young human visible face, messy black hair, sand-colored scarf, weathered grey-white stone armor with narrow gold trim, long torn sand cloth panels, black underclothes, long straight sword in character's anatomical right hand (screen left), open broken circular bypass shield/ring in anatomical left hand (screen right). Preserve slim proportions and all equipment identity. The sword remains a straight aligned blade held at grip, downward at the left, not detached or enlarged. Ring is handheld, never a halo. Same quiet standing pose, feet together enough to fit the slim reference. Upper-left lighting.
Style: match the detailed painted sprite master, crisp restrained outlines and readable color clusters, no smooth plastic 3D, no voxel or block forms, no redesign. Simplify tiny details for eventual 48-pixel character height without changing body shape.
Canvas is portrait 4:5, transparent RGBA. Character centered horizontally, entire head, sword and both boots visible, subject height exactly around 60% of canvas. Top of hair at 20% canvas height, soles at 80%. Keep broad transparent margins. No ground, shadow, background, glow, caption, grid, text or extra figures.

prompts.walk_initial:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset: an 8-frame WALK CYCLE sprite sheet for a 2D isometric game, based exactly on the supplied single character. This is one same character moving over time, NOT eight views or eight designs.
Layout: exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight evenly sized invisible cells, row-major temporal order. Wide 8:5 canvas. True transparent RGBA throughout; no text, numbers, borders, grid lines, shadows or ground. Each cell is identical portrait 4:5. Keep generous transparent spacing; no part touches a cell boundary. All 8 characters at the SAME SCALE: visible character about 60% of each cell height, hips centered at same horizontal point, ground-root projection at 80% cell height. Fixed orthographic camera looking slightly down, identical southwest three-quarter FRONT view in EVERY frame, nose points screen down-left. Do not rotate the body into a side or back view.
Identity: match supplied reference very closely: slim young human, messy black hair, visible face, sand scarf, layered weathered white stone armor with thin gold trim and tiny turquoise gems, black underclothes, hanging sand-and-black split cloth skirt, straight long sword in anatomical RIGHT hand on screen LEFT, open C-shaped ring shield in LEFT hand on screen RIGHT. Keep sword nearly vertical and close to body with a small natural swing. The weapon never changes hands, length, shape, or detaches from grip. Ring is visibly open at top, not a closed circle. Cloth stays close with restrained follow-through. No new clothing, armor or redesign.
Motion is a natural deliberate grounded WALK, not running or marching: alternate legs, visibly bend knees during swing, soft hip and shoulder counterrotation, relaxed elbows, small head bob. Maintain stable proportions across all cells, no individual resizing, no stretching.
Frame 1: anatomical right foot forward in heel contact, left foot behind pushing off; modest split stride.
Frame 2: weight settles onto right foot, right knee soft, left heel lifts behind.
Frame 3: right leg supports body; bent left knee passes forward beneath hips, left foot clearly lifted, not two feet on ground.
Frame 4: left lower leg extends for next heel contact, right heel begins rising; slightly higher hips.
Frame 5: left heel forward contacts ground, right foot behind; opposite half of frame 1.
Frame 6: weight settles on left foot; right heel lifts.
Frame 7: left leg supports body; bent right knee passes forward underneath, right foot lifted.
Frame 8: right lower leg extends toward next heel contact, left heel begins rising; connects naturally back to frame 1.
The eight poses must be genuinely different consecutive gait phases with alternating feet, not duplicates, not a sequence of torso translations. Front skirt panels separate naturally to reveal each knee; rigid shin armor follows the lower leg, knees remain joints.
Rendering: exactly the reference's crisp painterly retro game sprite, restrained edges and color clusters that remain readable at 48-pixel visible height. Preserve hair, face, stone/cloth distinction and upper-left light. No smooth 3D/plastic, no dramatic cape, no motion blur, no extra effects.
prompts.walk_correction:
Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve.
Edit this 4-column x 2-row sprite sheet into a correct alternating walk cycle. Keep the entire FIRST ROW unchanged. Keep the identity, face, hair, body scale, camera, sword, shield, hands and upper torso of ALL characters unchanged. Keep transparent background and exact 4x2 layout.
CRITICAL CHANGE: in the BOTTOM ROW, the wrong leg is leading. Fix the lower body and the hanging cloth of frames 5,6,7,8 so that they represent the OPPOSITE half of the gait to the top row.
For bottom-row frame 5 (leftmost): the LEG ON THE SHIELD SIDE (screen RIGHT, character's left leg) must extend FORWARD toward lower-left/front of scene, its boot visibly LOWEST on the canvas. The LEG ON THE SWORD SIDE (screen LEFT, character's right leg) trails BACK and its boot is visibly higher. Bend the right knee naturally. This must visibly reverse which leg is forward relative to top-left frame.
For bottom-row frame 6: support weight on SHIELD-SIDE left leg, with its boot still lowest; SWORD-SIDE right heel lifts behind.
For bottom-row frame 7: SHIELD-SIDE left leg supports, SWORD-SIDE right knee bends and passes forward, its boot raised. Existing bottom-row frame 7 is the closest example of the desired opposite leg emphasis.
For bottom-row frame 8: SWORD-SIDE right lower leg swings forward into the NEXT right heel contact, SHIELD-SIDE left leg begins pushing off, intermediate between frame 7 and top-left frame 1.
Preserve legs' anatomical attachment at hips and knees; do not swap armor, hands, sword or shield, and do not mirror the entire character. Split coat panels follow the changed legs, exposing both knees. Arms and weapon remain in their current hands. Normal restrained grounded walking, no jumping. No new items, no background, no text.
prompts.left_contact_attempt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Create ONE full-body walking pose of this exact character with the same camera, rendering, face, hair, costume, armor, sword and open ring shield, on transparent background.
He is facing southwest / down-left in a three-quarter front view.
VERY SPECIFIC POSE: His LEFT LEG, on the RING SHIELD side (the leg on viewer's RIGHT), takes a long step FORWARD. That left boot is closest to camera, lower and farther forward than the other boot. His RIGHT LEG, on the SWORD side (viewer's LEFT), stretches BACK BEHIND him, with its heel lifted and only toes near ground. This is an asymmetric LEFT-FOOT-FORWARD heel-contact walking pose. Keep both legs visibly separate, with the cloth split to show which thigh connects to which knee and boot. The left shin angles down and toward the front; the right leg goes diagonally back. No raised marching knee in this contact pose.
Keep anatomical right hand gripping sword on viewer's LEFT; keep left hand gripping open ring shield on viewer's RIGHT. No mirroring and no equipment swapping. Body leans very slightly forward, head and torso stable. Feet are on a 2:1 isometric ground plane, no ground drawn. Modest natural stride, sword down close to body, cloth follows legs with small motion.
Slim proportions identical to input, no chibi exaggeration, no wider armor, no redesign. Whole figure fully inside canvas with transparent margin. No captions, no multiple figures, no shadow.
prompts.opposite_contact:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied ONE character pose. Keep all pixels of head, torso, hands, sword and ring shield visually identical. Keep the SAME standing/support leg: the straight leg on IMAGE RIGHT below the shield remains the foreground leg, and the bent leg on IMAGE LEFT below the sword remains the rear leg.
Change only the lower leg pose into a walking heel-contact: extend the IMAGE-RIGHT foreground leg slightly forward so its boot is at lower right, heel touching ground and toe slightly raised. Swing the IMAGE-LEFT bent leg backward behind the body, with its boot higher and farther back, toe pointed down. Do NOT put the image-left boot at the bottom. The LOWEST boot must be the IMAGE-RIGHT boot, under the ring shield. The IMAGE-LEFT boot must be visibly higher, under the sword hand. Keep the hips, knees and armor anatomically connected. This is the opposite of right-leg-forward. Show a modest stride, not a lunge. Same face, hair, identity, camera angle, body scale and rendering style. Entire body and sword visible, generous transparent RGBA margins, no ground, no shadow, no text.
